decision.trend: Research on high-entropy alloys has been focused on understanding their thermodynamic properties, phase evolution, and mechanical behavior. Earlier studies have explored the use of computational methods, such as first-principles calculations and Monte Carlo simulations, to predict phase evolution and thermodynamic properties. Recent studies have also investigated the effects of alloying elements on the microstructure and properties of high-entropy alloys. The trend suggests a growing interest in using computational methods and experimental techniques to understand the behavior of high-entropy alloys and to design new materials with improved properties.

Additionally, the development of accurate and efficient methods for predicting the properties of high-entropy alloys remains a challenge.

decision.why: The next step in addressing the challenges associated with high-entropy alloys is to develop a machine learning-based approach that can accurately predict their thermodynamic properties and phase evolution. This approach can leverage the existing computational methods and experimental data to develop a predictive model that can guide the design of new high-entropy alloys with improved properties. The use of machine learning algorithms can help to identify patterns and correlations in the data that may not be apparent through traditional methods, and can provide a more efficient and accurate way to predict the behavior of high-entropy alloys.
